## Data Exploration

First, I am just taking a quick look at the data.

```{r}
# load packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# import data
superstore <- read_excel("data/superstore_data.xls")

# look at data, check size and structure 

names(superstore)
head(superstore)
dim(superstore) # 9994 rows, 21 columns (variables) 
str(superstore) # POSIXct means date/time values

# Postal Code should be a character string, not numeric
# use 'col_types = "guess"' so R can guess the rest of the columns 
# (should stay same as before) 
# but explicitly read the Postal Code column, column 12, as text 

superstore <- read_excel(
  "data/superstore_data.xls",
  col_types = c(
    rep("guess", 11),
    "text",
    rep("guess", 9)
  )
)

# check this
str(superstore)
str(superstore$`Postal Code`)
```

**Numeric Variables:**

- Row ID (doesn't really matter)
- Sales
- Quantity
- Discount
- Profit

**Categorical Variables:**

- Order ID
- Ship Mode
- Customer ID
- Customer Name
- Segment
- Country
- City
- State
- Postal Code
- Region
- Product ID
- Category
- Sub-Category
- Product Name

```{r}
# check for any missing values
colSums(is.na(superstore)) # none!
```

## Research Questions 

I am interested in 3 main questions: 

1) **Which states have the highest sales, number of orders, and number of customers?** 
2. **What do customers in these states buy most often?** 
3. **Are the sales in these states profitable?** 

### State Summary
```{r}
# summarize sales, profit, orders, and customers by state

# `n_distinct()` counts unique values instead of every row 

state_summary <- superstore |>
  group_by(State) |>
  summarize(
    total_sales = sum(Sales),
    total_profit = sum(Profit),
    profit_margin = total_profit / total_sales * 100,
    total_orders = n_distinct(`Order ID`),
    total_customers = n_distinct(`Customer ID`),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# show top 10 states by number of sales 

top_states <- state_summary |>
  arrange(desc(total_sales)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

top_states

# show top 10 states by number of orders
top_orders <- state_summary |>
  arrange(desc(total_orders)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

top_orders

# show top 10 states by number of customers
top_customers <- state_summary |>
  arrange(desc(total_customers)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

top_customers
```

### State and Category Summary
```{r}
state_cat_summary <- superstore |>
  group_by(State, Category) |>
  summarize(
    total_quantity = sum(Quantity),
    total_sales = sum(Sales),
    total_profit = sum(Profit),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# compare categories in the 10 highest-sales states
state_cat_summary |>
  filter(State %in% top_states$State) |>
  arrange(State, desc(total_quantity))
```

## Numerical Summaries by Product Category
```{r}
cat_num_sum <- superstore |>
  group_by(Category, `Sub-Category`) |>
  summarize(
    mean_sales = mean(Sales),
    median_sales = median(Sales),
    sd_sales = sd(Sales),
    
    mean_quantity = mean(Quantity),
    median_quantity = median(Quantity),
    sd_quantity = sd(Quantity),
    
    mean_profit = mean(Profit),
    median_profit = median(Profit),
    sd_profit = sd(Profit),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat_num_sum

```

## Graphical Summaries

### Bar Chart
```{r}
# Top 10 States by Total Sales (Q1)

ggplot(top_states, aes(
  x = reorder(State, total_sales),
  y = total_sales
)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 States by Total Sales",
    x = "State",
    y = "Total Sales ($)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Side-By-Side Bar Chart
```{r}
# Sales by Product Category Across Top States (Q1 & Q2)

state_cat_sales <- superstore |>
  filter(State %in% top_states$State) |>
  group_by(State, Category) |>
  summarize(
    total_sales = sum(Sales),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  state_cat_sales,
  aes(x = State, y = total_sales, fill = Category)
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Sales by Product Category Across Top 10 States",
    x = "State",
    y = "Total Sales ($)",
    fill = "Product Category"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Scatter Plot
```{r}
# Total Sales vs. Total Profit by State (Q3)

ggplot(state_summary, aes(
  x = total_sales,
  y = total_profit,
  color = total_profit
)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Total Sales vs. Total Profit by State",
    x = "Total Sales ($)",
    y = "Total Profit ($)",
    color = "Total Profit ($)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Box Plot
```{r}
# Profit Ditribution by Product Category (Q3)

ggplot(superstore, aes(
  x = Category,
  y = Profit,
  fill = Category
)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Profit Distribution by Product Category",
    x = "Product Category",
    y = "Profit ($)",
    fill = "Product Category"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Faceted Bar Chart
```{r}
# Quantity sold by sub-category across the top 10 states
top_state_subcat_sales <- superstore |>
  filter(State %in% top_states$State) |>
  group_by(Category, `Sub-Category`) |>
  summarize(
    total_quantity = sum(Quantity),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot quantity sold by product sub-category
ggplot(
  top_state_subcat_sales,
  aes(
    x = reorder(`Sub-Category`, total_quantity),
    y = total_quantity,
    fill = Category
  )
) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Category, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Quantity Sold by Product Sub-Category Across the Top 10 States",
    x = "Product Sub-Category",
    y = "Total Quantity Sold"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Heatmap
```{r}
# Heatmap of Sales by State and Product Category (Q1 & Q2)

ggplot(
  state_cat_sales,
  aes(
    x = State,
    y = Category,
    fill = total_sales
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Sales by State and Product Category",
    x = "State",
    y = "Product Category",
    fill = "Total Sales ($)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```
